scenes.tts: If the organizer sends a signal, the signal should be a substance. So kill the cells. Does it still work?
scenes.visual: Title card: Dead Tissue That Still Induces. A piece of organizer tissue beside a dish.
scenes.narration: If the organizer sends a signal, the signal should be a substance. So kill the cells. Does it still work?

scenes.tts: From nineteen thirty-three, Johannes Holtfreter froze, dried and heated pieces of newt embryos, some to boiling.
scenes.caption: From 1933, Johannes Holtfreter froze, dried and heated pieces of newt embryos, some to boiling.
scenes.visual: Credit: Johannes Holtfreter, from 1933. Three treatments on organizer pieces: frozen, dried, heated to boiling.
scenes.narration: From 1933, Johannes Holtfreter froze, dried and heated pieces of newt embryos, some to boiling.

scenes.tts: He placed them against early-gastrula ectoderm. On its own, that ectoderm became skin.
scenes.visual: Dish 1: ectoderm alone becomes flat skin. Dish 2: ectoderm pressed against a killed piece, outcome hidden.
scenes.narration: He placed them against early-gastrula ectoderm. On its own, that ectoderm became skin.

scenes.tts: Next to dead organizer, does the ectoderm become neural? And does a second axis form?
scenes.narration: Next to dead organizer, does the ectoderm become neural? And does a second axis form?

scenes.tts: The ectoderm often became neural. A living organizer was not needed for the neural response.
scenes.visual: Dish 2 reveals: the ectoderm becomes neural tissue. Tick next to neural.
scenes.narration: The ectoderm often became neural. A living organizer was not needed for the neural response.

scenes.tts: But in these tests, organizing did not survive. Killed tissue made ectoderm neural without building an organized second axis.
scenes.narration: But in these tests, organizing did not survive. Killed tissue made ectoderm neural without building an organized second axis.

scenes.tts: A factor is sufficient if it is enough, by itself, to produce an effect. It is necessary if that effect does not happen without it.
scenes.narration: A factor is sufficient if it is enough, by itself, to produce an effect. It is necessary if that effect does not happen without it.

scenes.tts: Dead organizer was sufficient to make ectoderm neural. But sufficient does not mean natural. Then the controls were run.
scenes.visual: Card: dead organizer, sufficient. A table titled Scores neural? begins.
scenes.narration: Dead organizer was sufficient to make ectoderm neural. But sufficient does not mean natural. Then the controls were run.

scenes.tts: Many other killed tissues induced too. So did ether extracts of amphibian tissue, in the nineteen thirties.
scenes.caption: Many other killed tissues induced too. So did ether extracts of amphibian tissue, in the 1930s.
scenes.visual: Table rows: other killed tissues, yes; ether extracts of amphibian tissue, yes. Credit: Waddington, Needham and Needham, by 1934.
scenes.narration: Many other killed tissues induced too. So did ether extracts of amphibian tissue, in the 1930s.

scenes.tts: Unrelated materials, from adult tissues to synthetic chemicals, induced in some cases.
scenes.visual: Table row: unrelated materials, from adult tissues to synthetic chemicals, in some cases.
scenes.narration: Unrelated materials, from adult tissues to synthetic chemicals, induced in some cases.

scenes.tts: In the nineteen forties, salamander ectoderm became neural with no organizer at all, or after brief damage.
scenes.caption: In the 1940s, salamander ectoderm became neural with no organizer at all, or after brief damage.
scenes.visual: Table row: salamander (Ambystoma) ectoderm, no organizer or brief damage, yes. Credit: Barth, then Holtfreter, 1940s.
scenes.narration: In the 1940s, salamander ectoderm became neural with no organizer at all, or after brief damage.

scenes.tts: When almost everything scores yes, a yes cannot name the signal.
scenes.visual: Full table: nearly every row says yes. On screen: When almost everything scores yes, a yes cannot name the signal.
scenes.narration: When almost everything scores yes, a yes cannot name the signal.

scenes.tts: Waddington described the trap. Perhaps competent ectoderm already holds a hidden tendency to become neural.
scenes.caption: C. H. Waddington described the trap. Perhaps competent ectoderm already holds a hidden tendency to become neural.
scenes.visual: Credit: C. H. Waddington. An ectoderm sheet, uniformly tinted, with a faint neural label that could be switched on anywhere.
scenes.narration: C. H. Waddington described the trap. Perhaps competent ectoderm already holds a hidden tendency to become neural.

scenes.tts: Then a substance might be the natural signal. Or it might merely injure the tissue, and release that tendency.
scenes.visual: Two arrows into the ectoderm: natural signal, or injury that releases the hidden tendency.
scenes.narration: Then a substance might be the natural signal. Or it might merely injure the tissue, and release that tendency.

scenes.tts: The salamander result is one explanation for why the chemical hunt stalled for decades.
scenes.visual: A search timeline from the 1930s onward, with no molecule named; the salamander row highlighted.
scenes.narration: The salamander result is one explanation for why the chemical hunt stalled for decades.

scenes.tts: Suppose neural is what ectoderm becomes when a brake is released. Then many injuries and chemicals that weaken it would be expected to induce too.
scenes.visual: A brake symbol on the ectoderm; several agents loosen it; each sheet turns neural.
scenes.narration: Suppose neural is what ectoderm becomes when a brake is released. Then many injuries and chemicals that weaken it would be expected to induce too.

scenes.tts: The next lesson shows frog ectoderm, its cells separated, becoming neural with no inducer at all.
scenes.visual: Preview card: next lesson. Frog ectoderm separated into single cells turns neural.
scenes.narration: The next lesson shows frog ectoderm, its cells separated, becoming neural with no inducer at all.

scenes.tts: So neighbours can set a cell's fate, while it can still answer. What the signal is comes next.
scenes.visual: Closing card: neighbours set fate while cells can answer. Next: what is the signal?
scenes.narration: So neighbours can set a cell's fate, while it can still answer. What the signal is comes next.
